name: Google Antigravity

allow.note: A decision of allow is applied without a prompt. Observed indirectly: every gated call whose decision was not a block proceeded, and the host reported the tool result back.

ask.note: The verdict lands, but whether it reaches a person depends on the host. With the user’s autoExecutionPolicy set to CASCADE_COMMANDS_AUTO_EXECUTION_EAGER, an ask on `run_command` and on `write_to_file` executed with no prompt shown. That is the host honouring its own auto-execution setting, and it is exactly why a floored action must not use this verdict.

deny.note: Observed: with a deny rule in place, the command was blocked and the model was told "The command was denied by the pre-tool hook rule: LeastGrant: LeastGrant blocked this: you set a rule to always block this." The reason string reaches the model verbatim.

forceAsk.note: The claim this integration exists for, verified live and under the hardest available conditions. In the same session where an ordinary ask executed with no prompt because auto-execution was set to EAGER, a force_ask on a credential read stopped the call dead: the UI showed "Waiting for user input — Allow read access to this path?" with LeastGrant’s own reason beneath it, offered "Yes, and always allow", and no PostToolUse fired. The file’s contents never reached the model. The agent then retried through run_command and was floored again.

onCrash.note: REFUTES the earlier binary read. A hook exiting 3 does not fail open: the call was blocked and the model was told "The command could not be executed because the pre-tool hook failed: JSON hook \"jsonhook__leastgrant_PreToolUse_0_0\" failed: command failed: exit status 3". The static read of applyPreToolHooks logging and continuing describes iteration over the remaining hooks, not the caller, which aborts.

onTimeout.note: Also fails closed. A handler sleeping past its 10s timeout blocked the call, and the UI reported "All tool calls are currently being blocked by this hook."

timeoutDefaultSeconds.note: Per handler, set by the integer `timeout` field. 0 or negative silently becomes 30; there is no unlimited option.

canFailClosed.note: Not a setting — it is the default. Crash, timeout, unparseable stdout, JSON without a decision, and an unrecognised decision string all block the call. The one way through is an empty stdout with exit 0, which the runtime treats as "no hook result" and lets the call proceed.

shell.note: run_command reaches PreToolUse with CommandLine, Cwd, IsDaemon, WaitMsBeforeAsync and the tool’s own toolAction/toolSummary. Both gated and floored live.

fileRead.note: view_file and find_by_name both reach PreToolUse before execution. A force_ask on view_file of a credential file blocked it with nothing reaching the model.

fileWrite.note: write_to_file reaches PreToolUse with TargetFile, CodeContent, Description and Overwrite. Gated live.

mcp.note: MCP arrives as a single call_mcp_tool carrying {ServerName, ToolName, Arguments}. The adapter rebuilds the engine’s own mcp__server__tool identity from it, so MCP calls get the same tiering, signature and secret guards as on any other agent. Observed live: before that mapping every MCP call was force_ask because the call was unaccountable; after it, an ordinary call asks and can become familiar, and a credential-bearing argument still floors.

subagentSpawn.note: invoke_subagent, define_subagent and manage_subagents exist as tool names in the runtime, but no subagent tool was invoked during the live run — the model answered the request directly instead — so nothing has been observed. Not claimed as gated.

interception.note: Unusually broad. Matcher names are derived mechanically from an internal step-type enum of roughly 115 values.

postToolUse.note: PostToolUse fires for each completed call, carries toolCall, stepIdx and error (empty string on success), and accepts {} as its result. Observed for run_command, list_dir, find_by_name and write_to_file.

canModifyInput.note: The shipped local docs describe input rewriting; the public web docs list only decision/reason/permission and are incomplete here.

exposesMode.note: The captured payloads carry conversationId, workspacePaths, transcriptPath, artifactDirectoryPath, modelName, stepIdx and toolCall — and no permission-mode field. LeastGrant cannot tell an attended session from an unattended one, which is why the eager auto-execution behaviour above is invisible to it.

modes.askSurvivesNote: force_ask survives everything, which is why the mode is not needed to decide whether an ask will land.

upstreamLimitations: The hook engine installs only when the server-delivered experiment flag json-hooks-enabled is true. It is per-session, not persisted, not readable and not overridable from the client, so LeastGrant cannot tell an enforcing session from an unenforced one.

An ordinary ask does not necessarily reach a person. Observed live: with autoExecutionPolicy = CASCADE_COMMANDS_AUTO_EXECUTION_EAGER, an ask on a shell command and on a file write both executed with no prompt. Only force_ask is reliable, which is why LeastGrant floors to it.

force_ask is silently downgraded to an allow when the host sets auto_interaction_behavior=ALLOW_ALL. ResolveAutoInteraction runs before any prompt is registered and the hook gets no signal. Not exercised live; read from the runtime.

An empty stdout with exit 0 lets the call through. The runtime trims the output and treats an empty result as "no hook result", so a handler that stands aside silently is an allow. Every other failure mode blocks.
The runtime reads hooks from four workspace roots — .agents, _agents, .agent and _agent — and from plugins/<name>/hooks.json. Any of them can add a handler; the published docs mention only .agents.

Two of the six accepted verdicts are undocumented. auto_approve is accepted by the runtime and returns a silent allow with no prompt, appearing in neither the published docs nor the hooks guide embedded in the binary; deny_unless_prior_grant appears on the web page but not in that embedded guide.

deny and ask do not have the same reach. deny is enforced in the tool-call converter, before the permission manager; ask and force_ask are read only by the permissions package, which a step reaches only if it declares permission targets.

The runtime supports six hook events — PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreInvocation, PostInvocation, Stop and SessionStart. Stop carries its own decision field. LeastGrant registers only the two tool events, so the others are unmediated.

Prompt-mode handlers exist (HookHandlerConfig.prompt, executePromptModeHook) despite the embedded guide saying only command handlers are supported. A prompt handler is a model deciding a permission question.
An unanswered force_ask blocks its conversation indefinitely. That is the intended behaviour of the verdict and it is also a way to wedge a session.
leastgrantLimitations: Subagent tools are not verified. invoke_subagent, define_subagent and manage_subagents exist in the runtime, but no subagent call was made during the live run, so LeastGrant has not been observed gating one.
LeastGrant does not model the PreInvocation, PostInvocation, Stop or SessionStart events, and does not use the overwrite field that lets a hook rewrite a tool call’s arguments.
Verified on Windows only, through the Desktop Hub. The Unix launch form (sh -c) is not present in this build — GOOS is a compile-time constant — and the IDE surface was not exercised.

Network and web tools are unverified. The model answered a search request from its own knowledge rather than calling a tool, so search_web and read_url_content have never been observed reaching the hook.

live.what: Driven through the real signed-in Antigravity Desktop window over CDP, in a disposable project with a synthetic .env, with a transparent wrapper capturing the wire bytes. Observed: the host invoking jsonhook__leastgrant_PreToolUse_0_0 by name; real PreToolUse and PostToolUse payloads for run_command, view_file, list_dir, find_by_name and write_to_file; deny blocking a command with LeastGrant’s reason shown to the model; force_ask stopping a credential read and raising a human prompt carrying LeastGrant’s reason, in the same session where an ordinary ask had been auto-executed; and the full failure matrix — non-zero exit, timeout, unparseable stdout, decision-less JSON and unknown decision all block, empty stdout allows.

transport.what: The real invocation was observed rather than reproduced: cmd /c, working directory set to the directory containing hooks.json, payload delivered on stdin as flat protojson camelCase with no BOM, ANTIGRAVITY_CONVERSATION_ID injected into the child environment, handler named jsonhook__leastgrant_<name>_<event>_<group>_<index>. Round trip measured at 92–121 ms.

contract.what: Contract re-derived from the shipped 153 MB Go runtime by parsing its pclntab into 166,036 symbols, disassembling the decision sites, and parsing the embedded hooks.proto FileDescriptorProto. Established at instruction level: force_ask skips the permission-cache check() call and zeroes its result before forcing ASK, where ask honours a cached grant; a missing decision becomes deny via the legacy allow_tool bool; a non-zero exit zeroes the stdout slice and the caller fails open; timeout 0 or negative becomes 30. Corrected two facts LeastGrant had wrong: PostToolHookArgs carries tool_call and result as well as step_idx, and the runtime reads hooks from four workspace roots plus plugins.

mechanism: A named hook in ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json with `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` groups, matcher `*`. There is no event name on the wire — the event is a protobuf oneof and both events carry `toolCall` — so LeastGrant labels its own handlers with `--event pre` and `--event post` rather than guessing from the payload.

controlPaths.what: the global hook definitions — where LeastGrant installs itself
workspace hook definitions. The runtime reads FOUR roots — .agents, _agents, .agent and _agent — and any of them can install a handler that runs on every later tool call
the second of the four workspace customization roots the runtime walks
the third of the four workspace customization roots the runtime walks
the fourth of the four workspace customization roots the runtime walks
plugins are a third hook source: GetJSONHooks calls GetAllPlugins and parses plugins/<name>/hooks.json, so installing a plugin installs its hooks

userSettings.globalPermissionGrants.allow — the host’s own standing-approval list. An agent that appends one entry grants itself permanent approval for that tool, invisibly to LeastGrant and surviving our uninstall
which MCP servers the runtime starts and wires in
per-project resources and settings, including which folders are in scope
the folder-to-project registry that decides which of those applies here
IDE-level settings shared across the Gemini tools, read at startup before any project is chosen
built-in skills — instructions a later session loads and follows
persisted memory handed to later sessions as context
implicit context the runtime accumulates and replays into later sessions
cached MCP tool schemas, one per tool, holding the description of that tool the model is given
